key_insight: D-Gun-sprayed NiCrAlY provided higher hardness and better corrosion resistance, while 80Ni20Cr showed lower erosion mass loss on Al 6061-T6.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection should match the dominant damage mode: NiCrAlY for hardness and saline corrosion resistance, or 80Ni20Cr for erosion resistance under the tested conditions.
method: Deposited 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 using detonation gun thermal spraying.
Characterised microstructure, phases, roughness and hardness using SEM-EDS, XRD, AFM and nanoindentation.
Evaluated saline corrosion, water contact angle and solid-particle erosion.
evidence_signal: NiCrAlY reached 7895.36 MPa hardness versus 780.11 MPa for 80Ni20Cr, with corrosion rates of 0.00567 and 0.01427 mm/year, respectively, versus 0.5185 mm/year for bare aluminium.
watch_item: Room-temperature corrosion tests in 3.5 wt% NaCl and one erosion condition (90° impact, 40 m/s, 5 min) do not establish long-term service performance.
paper_title: Microstructure and surface performance of detonation gun sprayed 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 substrate for structural applications
